articles.title: Chainflip Says Attacker Also Took 122.86 Bitcoin, Offers 10% Bounty
articles.excerpt: The swap protocol's own tally puts the loss near $12.3 million, up from $4.86 million first traced on Ethereum. Its return deadline is 1:38 p.m. ET Monday.
articles.body_md:
Chainflip said Saturday the attacker who drained its vaults also took 122.86 bitcoin, lifting the loss to about $12.3 million at 5:51 p.m. ET prices. The project offered a 10% bounty for the rest.

That is more than double the roughly $4.86 million first traced from its Ethereum vault early Saturday. In a [message to the attacker](https://chainflip.io/return) on its website, Chainflip Labs listed 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3,249,631 USDC and 758,141 USDT. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainflip-offers-10-bounty-for-return-of-stolen-funds) also reported the bitcoin figure.

Black Mint valued the haul using [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) prices at 5:51 p.m. ET, with bitcoin at $60,060 and ether at $1,679. The bitcoin alone comes to about $7.4 million.

**Keep 10%, return 90%**

Chainflip said in an [X post](https://x.com/Chainflip/status/2124221824116703335) at 2:22 p.m. ET that it had sent the offer as an [onchain message](https://mempool.space/tx/0f75dbd50f247d4d29ffb5d19dae9907f0322f9ef504720b7e27d2453624f004) to the address holding the bitcoin. The terms ask for 110.58 BTC and 2,618.1 ETH by 1:38 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 23. If both arrive, Chainflip says it will treat the case as a white-hat recovery and withdraw its complaints to law enforcement.

**What Chainflip says it found**

The company said it traced how the attack was set up: funding through the Tornado Cash mixer on Nov. 11, a purchase of FLIP tokens and a validator account registered on Nov. 20. It said it has identified how the signing credentials were exposed and has blocked that route. Those are Chainflip's statements. It has not published a full post-mortem, and no one has been named or charged.

**How the vaults are guarded**

Chainflip's validators must bond FLIP as collateral to join the network, according to its [documentation](https://docs.chainflip.io/protocol/protocol-overview). The vaults move funds only with an aggregate key controlled by 100 of 150 validators through a threshold signature scheme, a method that splits signing power so no single party holds it whole.

FLIP traded at $0.308 at 5:51 p.m. ET, down 35.9% in 24 hours, with a market value of about $26.5 million, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/chainflip) data show.

*In our opinion: The new tally puts the loss at nearly half of FLIP's entire $26.5 million market value. Chainflip's posts and return page don't say who will cover the shortfall: users, liquidity providers or the company. Monday's 1:38 p.m. ET deadline is the first date to watch, and the post-mortem explaining the breach is the second.*

articles.title: Kalshi Faces Monday Hearing on NY Order After Judge Denies CFTC Bid
articles.excerpt: A state judge hears New York's restraining-order request at 11:30 a.m. ET. Kalshi says the wording could close its exchange everywhere; the state says it won't.
articles.body_md:
A federal judge on Friday denied the CFTC's second emergency request to stop New York's case against Kalshi. That leaves a state judge to hear New York's restraining-order bid at 11:30 a.m. ET Monday.

U.S. District Judge Lorna Schofield ruled after a telephone hearing Friday evening, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-21-kalshi-faces-monday-hearing-on-new-york-order-it-says-would-shut-down-its-exchange-nationwide-444813) and [Gambling Insider](https://www.gamblinginsider.com/news/204997/cftc-emergency-tro-denied-new-york-kalshi) reported. Gambling Insider said she found the agency had not shown a strong chance of winning its argument that federal commodities law overrides state gambling rules; The Block cited a letter from James' office describing the same finding.

**Why the scope matters**

Kalshi is headquartered in New York. The state's proposed order would bar it from operating within or from New York, both outlets reported. The Block said it also covers contracts offered to New Yorkers.

Kalshi's lawyers told the state court that because of that wording, the order would probably force all open positions to be closed, [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/US/kalshi-prediction-market-crippled-judge-grants-restraining-order/story?id=138329957) reported. A CFTC lawyer told Schofield the order would shut Kalshi down nationwide. New York's attorney general's office replied that it is not seeking a nationwide shutdown: Kalshi could still offer lawful futures and swaps, it said.

**The state's case**

Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi in July. She alleges it breaks state laws that bar betting on games involving New York college teams and sports betting by anyone under 21, ABC reported. Kalshi says its contracts are derivatives under the CFTC's exclusive oversight, so state gambling laws don't apply.

**How the fight works**

A temporary restraining order is a short court order that freezes conduct until a fuller hearing. Kalshi is a designated contract market, an exchange registered with the CFTC. The dispute turns on preemption, the question of whether a federal law, here the Commodity Exchange Act, overrides state rules.

Federal appeals courts have split on that question. Three have ruled against Kalshi and one in its favor, according to Gambling Insider and The Block. Justice Melissa Crane of the New York County Supreme Court will hear Monday's request.

*In our opinion: Monday's hearing turns on two small words, "from New York," and a lot of open positions ride on them. If the order reaches past state lines, customers in every state carry the risk; if it covers only New Yorkers, the state gets its rules and Kalshi keeps running elsewhere. Watch the scope Justice Crane writes, then whether either side files an appeal.*

articles.title: Upbit, Bithumb Halt CYBER Transfers After Unexpected Token Minting
articles.excerpt: Cyber says CYBER was minted on Solana and then moved out of its bridge's Ethereum lockbox. The token traded 7.9% lower over 24 hours at 5:51 p.m. ET.
articles.body_md:
South Korean exchanges Upbit and Bithumb suspended CYBER deposits and withdrawals shortly after noon ET Saturday. The token sat at $0.216 at 5:51 p.m. ET, 7.9% below its level a day earlier, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/cyberconnect) data show.

The halts followed what the Cyber project called "unexpected minting" of CYBER on Solana, "followed by a transfer of CYBER out of the bridge's Ethereum lockbox," it said in an [X post](https://x.com/BuildOnCyber/status/2124207519581327394) at 1:25 p.m. ET. Cyber said its team is checking which assets and bridge routes are affected and asked users to hold off for now.

[The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-11-21-cyber-investigating-suspected-1-million-bridge-exploit-as-upbit-bithumb-freeze-transfers-444810) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/cyber-warns-against-bridge-use-after-unexpected-minting) reported that Cyber urged users to stay off its bridge and avoid depositing CYBER to exchanges. The Block reported that the post also told users they don't need to migrate tokens, connect wallets or sign anything.

**What the exchanges did**

Bithumb's [notice](https://feed.bithumb.com/notice/1655756) set its halt for 2:18 a.m. Sunday Korea time, or 12:18 p.m. ET, citing a suspected security problem. Trading stays open, and the exchange warned of sharp price swings during the freeze. Upbit stopped CYBER transfers on the Ethereum network at 2:08 a.m. Korea time, [EconomyBloc](https://economybloc.com/article/126356/) reported from its notice. Neither exchange gave a restart date.

**How a bridge lockbox works**

Many tokens that live on more than one blockchain use a lock-and-mint bridge. Tokens are locked in a contract on one chain, here Ethereum, while matching tokens are created on another, such as Solana. The design depends on the two sides staying equal. Tokens minted without a matching lock can be sent back across to release real ones.

Cyber has not said what caused the minting or how many tokens were affected. The project, formerly CyberConnect, runs an Ethereum layer-2 network for social apps, according to its [website](https://cyber.co). CYBER's market value was about $13.2 million at 5:51 p.m. ET.

*In our opinion: The open question is whether every CYBER token in circulation is still backed one for one across chains. Holders who keep tokens on exchanges are waiting on the same answer, since Bithumb says transfers resume only once the network is stable. Cyber's next update should say how many tokens left the lockbox and how the bridge will be secured.*

articles.title: Russia's Crypto Exchange Rule Takes Effect Sunday; MOEX Eyes Dec. 1
articles.excerpt: The Bank of Russia registered Moscow Exchange's digital-currency trading rules on Nov. 19. MOEX plans pilot bitcoin, ether and USDT trades from Dec. 1.
articles.body_md:
A Bank of Russia rule that lets exchanges run organized crypto trading takes effect Sunday, Nov. 22. Three days earlier, on Nov. 19, the central bank registered Moscow Exchange's trading rules for a new digital-currency section.

Under the [ordinance](https://www.cbr.ru/eng/press/event/?id=32975), one condition applies: an exchange may start crypto trading only after the central bank agrees to its trading rules. The Nov. 19 [registration decision](https://www.cbr.ru/rbr/rbr_fr/doc?id=52870) covers Moscow Exchange's trading rulebook, including a new part for its digital-currency market section. Two days before that, the bank registered the exchange's [admission rules](https://www.cbr.ru/rbr/rbr_fr/doc?id=52859) for the same section, which set who can join as a trading member.

**What exchanges must do**

The ordinance requires exchanges to register every trading participant, such as brokers and trust managers, keep registers of orders and deals, and publish current, weighted-average, market and closing prices. Results go to the central bank the same way stock and bond data do, the bank said. [Vedomosti](https://www.vedomosti.ru/finance/news/2026/11/11/1244511-torgi-kriptovalyutami) reported the same terms.

**How the Moscow market is built**

Moscow Exchange said in a [Nov. 2 release](https://www.moex.com/n105654) that it plans to let brokers and other firms trade bitcoin, ether and Tether's USDT from Dec. 1, starting with pilot deals and adding firms as they are ready. Trades will run on its stock-market systems from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time.

Its clearing arm, the National Clearing Centre, will stand between buyer and seller. That central counterparty guarantees each trade settles, same day or next day, so traders don't carry each other's default risk. Ordinary investors must pass a test and can buy no more than 300,000 rubles a year through one broker, the exchange said.

**The sanctions backdrop**

The U.S. Treasury [sanctioned](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2404) Moscow Exchange and the National Clearing Centre in June 2024. Neither the exchange's release nor the central bank's notices address the U.S. measures.

Bitcoin was at $60,060 at 5:51 p.m. ET, 1.9% higher than a day earlier, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show.

*In our opinion: The paperwork is now mostly in place, and the open question is how many brokers connect by Dec. 1. Russian buyers gain a licensed domestic route, but the 300,000-ruble cap keeps retail volume small by design. With U.S. sanctions on both the exchange and its clearing house, the first pilot trades will mostly measure demand at home.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Climbs Back to $60,000 After Dropping Near $55,700 Overnight
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin rose about 8.6% from its 1 a.m. ET low, while U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $124.5 million on Friday and about $1.25 billion for the week.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000 on Saturday morning, about 8.6% above an overnight low near $55,711, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) hourly data show. It traded at $60,032 at 11:49 a.m. ET, up 1% from the same time Friday.

The low came around 1 a.m. ET. By 9 a.m. the price had reached $60,512, the top of the rebound on CoinGecko's hourly series. Kraken's own BTC/USD market traced a similar path: a low of $55,100 in the 1 a.m. hour and a high of $60,883 in the 9 a.m. hour, according to the exchange's [public price data](https://api.kraken.com/0/public/OHLC?pair=XBTUSD&interval=60).

**ETF investors pulled $1.25 billion this week**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $124.5 million on Friday, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show. That number is still missing BlackRock's IBIT, the biggest fund, which Farside hadn't filled in by midday Saturday. With Friday's partial figure, the funds lost about $1.25 billion over the week. Monday was the only day with a net inflow, at $7.9 million.

How the flow numbers work: when investors cash out of an ETF, the fund redeems shares and its bitcoin holdings shrink. A net outflow means more money left the funds that day than came in. Source: Farside Investors.

**Sentiment is still near the bottom of the scale**

The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) read 12 on Saturday, inside its "Extreme Fear" band. It was 10 on Thursday. Alternative.me builds the 0-to-100 score from inputs that include price volatility, trading volume and social media activity.

*In our opinion: An 8.6% bounce on a Saturday morning looks good on a chart. The number worth chasing is Farside's next update, which fills in IBIT's Friday figure and shows whether any of the $1.25 billion that left the funds this week is walking back in. Weekend rallies don't need ETF buyers. Monday's do.*

articles.title: Kraken Says Trades Stand After Bitcoin Hit C$24,250 on CAD Pair
articles.excerpt: Kraken's BTC/CAD market fell about 72% below its later level overnight. Kraken found no breach; Blockstream's Adam Back blamed its USD/CAD market.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin traded as low as C$24,250 on Kraken's Canadian-dollar market early Saturday, about 72% below the C$85,400 the same pair showed at 11 a.m. ET. Kraken said every executed trade will stand.

The exchange said heavy selling hit its CAD pairs starting around 3 p.m. ET Friday and pushed prices "well below other markets." In a [post from Kraken Support](https://x.com/krakensupport/status/2124098562443354591) at 6:12 a.m. ET Saturday, it said: "Our platform processed every order correctly, and our security teams found no sign of a breach or compromised accounts. Executed trades stand."

**The slide took about 12 hours**

Kraken's [public price data](https://api.kraken.com/0/public/OHLC?pair=XBTCAD&interval=60) show the BTC/CAD pair's hourly low falling from C$61,880 at 4 p.m. ET Friday to C$36,700 at 1 a.m. Saturday, then to C$24,250 in the 3 a.m. hour. About 77 bitcoin changed hands on the pair in that hour. By 5 a.m. the low was back above C$68,000. [CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/kraken-says-trades-stand-after-bitcoin-sold-at-24250-canadian/) also reported the C$24,250 low.

Over the same hours, Kraken's BTC/USD market bottomed at $55,100.

**One explanation, not yet confirmed by Kraken**

Adam Back, chief executive of Blockstream, [said on X](https://x.com/adam3us/status/2124094297884766353) that the cause was Kraken's USD/CAD market, where he said the "local spot FX market-maker ran out of money" and the rate moved away from the market rate of 1.434. Kraken's statement did not give a cause or say who was selling.

How a local price can break away: each trading pair has its own order book (the list of open bids and offers). If buyers on one pair run thin, sellers fill against lower and lower bids. Traders can normally buy the cheap coin and sell it elsewhere, which pulls prices back together, but only as fast as they can move Canadian dollars in and out.

As of 11:50 a.m. ET, Kraken had not published a cause for the gap or said who was selling.

articles.title: BTCS Says It Can't Rule Out Liquidation of $54 Million Aave Loan
articles.excerpt: The Nasdaq-listed ether holder put its Aave debt at $54 million against $111 million of crypto. Its shares closed Friday at 65.3 cents, down 12.2%.
articles.body_md:
BTCS, a Nasdaq-listed company that holds ether, owed about $54 million on the Aave lending protocol as of Nov. 19 and said it can't promise the loan won't be liquidated, according to an [8-K filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1436229/000149315226053286/form8-k.htm) with the SEC.

"We can provide no assurance as to the future amount of our borrowings, the value of our collateral, or that a liquidation will not occur," the company said in the statement, which it first posted on social media after investor questions.

**What BTCS owes and owns**

The filing lists about $111 million of crypto, valued at an ether price of $1,775, against the $54 million Aave debt and about $18 million of senior secured convertible notes (loans that can turn into shares). Ether traded at about $1,682 at 11:49 a.m. ET Saturday, roughly 5% below the price BTCS used, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum) data show.

BTCS shares closed Friday at 65.3 cents, down 12.2%, [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BTCS/) data show. That gave the company a market value of about $34.6 million. [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/21/ether-treasury-firm-btcs-warns-sec-its-usd54-million-aave-loan-could-be-liquidated) also reported the filing and the share move.

The company said it borrows stablecoins against part of its ether to fund liquidity pools run through Imperium, its DeFi business. "We may increase borrowings when the value of our ETH collateral rises and reduce borrowings when it falls," it said.

**How an Aave liquidation works**

Aave gives every loan a health factor: collateral value times a liquidation threshold set by Aave governance, divided by the debt, per [Aave's documentation](https://aave.com/help/borrowing/liquidations). Below 1, the loan can be liquidated. An outside liquidator repays part of the debt and takes the same value of collateral plus a bonus. Up to half the debt can go in one step, or all of it if the health factor drops to 0.95 or lower.

The filing doesn't give the loan's health factor or the ether price that would trigger liquidation.

*In our opinion: The number investors still don't have is the liquidation price, and that figure decides how much room BTCS has left. Ether already sits about 5% under the $1,775 the company used, and its $34.6 million market value is smaller than the $54 million it owes on Aave. The next update on that debt, in a filing or a post, is the one to read closely.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by an AI Code Scanner
articles.excerpt: Versions 30.5 and 31.3 fix CVE-2026-117348, a medium-severity flaw. The 29.x series stays exposed because it no longer gets fixes.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin Core released versions 30.5 and 31.3 on Friday to fix a medium-severity bug that let one peer freeze a node for more than a dozen seconds per message, according to the project's [security advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/).

The flaw, CVE-2026-117348, affects versions 29.0 to 29.5, 30.0 to 30.4 and 31.0 to 31.2. Version 32.1, released Oct. 27, already had the fix. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not be patched, the advisory said.

**Repeated IDs, Repeated Work**

A node is a computer that checks bitcoin transactions and blocks and passes them along. Sometimes it receives an orphan: a transaction spending coins from a parent the node hasn't seen yet. It holds the orphan and asks peers for the missing parents.

Peers announce transactions in batches of up to 50,000 entries, and Bitcoin Core did not skip duplicates. An attacker sending an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then its ID 50,000 times in one batch, forced the node to repeat the same lookups.

"Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds," the advisory said. During that time the node handles nothing else, including new blocks. The fix makes it process each announced transaction once. [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/21/bitcoin-nodes-could-be-stalled-by-repeating-one-id-50-000-times-ai-found-the-bug) that an exchange on an affected node might credit deposits late, and a miner could work from an outdated view of the chain.

**Credit Goes to Project Loupe**

The advisory credits an automated scan by a large language model, the type of AI behind chatbots, run through Elias Rohrer's Project Loupe at Spiral. Spiral is the open-source development unit of Jack Dorsey's Block, per CoinDesk. Developer Gregory Sanders checked it and wrote the fix. A second reporter, credited as Stutxo, flagged the same issue Aug. 4.

The advisory's timeline dates Loupe's report to July 8. The fix entered the main code Aug. 6 and reached the 30.x and 31.x branches Nov. 17. Both releases are on [GitHub](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/releases).

*In our opinion: this bug sat in the code from version 29.0 until a machine read the fine print closely enough to spot it, and a human confirmed it. The exposure falls on anyone running 29.0 through 31.2, from hobby nodes to exchange back ends, and 29.x users get no patch at all. The scoreboard to watch is the advisory page: if Loupe's name keeps showing up in the credits, AI scanners are earning a regular seat at the security table.*

articles.title: Chainflip Halts Swaps and Withdrawals Over Possible Vault Exploit
articles.excerpt: Security monitor Defimon Alerts said about $4.86 million left Chainflip's Ethereum vault. The FLIP token fell 39.8% in 24 hours.
articles.body_md:
Chainflip put its cross-chain swap protocol into "full safe mode" early Saturday, disabling deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quotes over what it called "a potential exploit affecting Chainflip vaults," the project said in a [post on X](https://x.com/Chainflip/status/2124068986845532605) at 4:14 a.m. ET.

About 100 minutes earlier, at 2:33 a.m. ET, the security monitor [Defimon Alerts](https://x.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2124043470151004633) said Chainflip's Ethereum vault had been swept of 520.2 ether, 3.25 million USDC and 758,000 USDT, which it valued at about $4.86 million. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/chainflip-halts-swaps-over-potential-vault-exploit) also reported the $4.86 million figure. Chainflip has not published a loss figure.

**Defimon Points to Signing Credentials**

Defimon labeled the incident a compromise of the vault's aggregate signing credentials. It said the funds moved to a newly created wallet. That is the monitor's assessment. Chainflip had not confirmed a cause as of 6 a.m. ET.

**How Chainflip Holds Funds**

Chainflip lets users swap coins across blockchains, such as bitcoin for ether, without wrapped tokens. According to its [documentation](https://docs.chainflip.io/protocol/protocol-overview), a network of 150 validators jointly holds aggregate keys through a threshold signature scheme. That method splits control of a signing credential among many parties so none of them holds it whole.

Those credentials control vaults: simple wallets or smart contracts on each supported chain. A blockchain accepts any transfer that carries a valid signature from the vault.

**FLIP Falls 39.8%**

Chainflip's FLIP token traded at $0.287 at 5:54 a.m. ET, down 39.8% in 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/chainflip). It was near $0.48 on Friday evening. Its market value was about $24.7 million.

Chainflip said it is investigating and "will share updates here as we learn more."

*In our opinion: so far the only official word is a short post with no loss figure, no cause and no restart date. Until safe mode lifts, nobody can move funds through the protocol, and FLIP holders have already absorbed a 39.8% drop. The document to wait for is Chainflip's post-mortem, which should say whether the signing credentials were compromised and how the vaults will be secured before swaps resume.*

articles.excerpt: BEA publishes October PCE and revised third-quarter GDP at 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday. U.S. stock markets close Thursday and at 1 p.m. Friday.
articles.body_md:
October's PCE inflation data and a second estimate of third-quarter GDP come out at 8:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, Nov. 25, according to the [Bureau of Economic Analysis release schedule](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule). Both land a day before Thanksgiving.

**The Fed's Preferred Inflation Gauge**

The PCE price index tracks what people in the U.S. pay for goods and services. The Fed's 2% inflation goal is [measured with it](https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/economy_14400.htm). In September, PCE prices were up 3.6% from a year earlier, or 3.1% excluding food and energy, [BEA said](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-september-2026).

Fed Governor Lisa Cook said in a [speech](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20261120a.htm) on Friday that the 12-month PCE change for October is estimated at 3.8%, based on data released last week. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75%-4% in September, she said.

The first GDP estimate showed the economy growing at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second, according to [BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-3rd-quarter-2026). Wednesday's report updates that figure.

**Day by Day**

- **Monday, Nov. 23:** Treasury sells $69 billion of 2-year notes, per [TreasuryDirect](https://www.treasurydirect.gov/auctions/upcoming/).
- **Tuesday, Nov. 24:** $70 billion of 5-year securities.
- **Wednesday, Nov. 25:** GDP and PCE at 8:30 a.m.; $44 billion of 7-year securities; the Fed's [Beige Book](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/beige-book-default.htm), a summary of business conditions gathered by each of the 12 regional Fed banks, at 2 p.m.
- **Thursday, Nov. 26:** Thanksgiving. Stock markets are closed, and the Fed's [calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/calendar.htm) moves that day's statistical releases to Friday.
- **Friday, Nov. 27:** NYSE markets close early at 1 p.m. ET, per the [exchange](https://www.nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars).

**How Rates Reach Crypto**

Higher interest rates raise the return on cash and bonds. That makes assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin, harder to justify for some investors. The Fed's next decision comes after its Dec. 8-9 meeting, per its calendar.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had about $1.25 billion of net outflows from Monday through Friday, before BlackRock's IBIT reported its Friday figure, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/). Bitcoin traded at $57,927 at 5:54 a.m. ET Saturday, down 6.6% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: Wednesday carries most of the week's freight, with inflation, growth, a $44 billion auction and the Beige Book all landing before anyone carves a turkey. The bar for October's PCE is Cook's 3.8% estimate, against September's 3.6%. The Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting will have that number in hand, and so will anyone holding bonds or bitcoin.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Falls to $55,483, Its Lowest Price Since September 2024
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin slid below its July low of $57,734 late Friday and traded at $56,397 at 11:53 p.m. ET, down 8.2% in 24 hours, as ETF outflows continued.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell as low as $55,483.28 on Bitstamp late Friday, its lowest price since September 2024. It traded at $56,397 at 11:53 p.m. ET, down 8.2% in 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

Ether was at $1,564, down 9.2% over the same window, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

**Below the July low**

Friday's drop took bitcoin under its low for 2026. [Bitstamp's daily price data](https://www.bitstamp.net/api/v2/ohlc/btcusd/?step=86400&limit=1000&start=1717200000) put the previous 2026 low at $57,734.63 on July 1. The last time bitcoin traded below Friday's low was Sept. 9, 2024, when it touched $54,587. [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/21/bitcoin-tanks-below-usd57-000-for-the-first-time-in-two-years-and-its-not-alone) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-falls-lowest-level-since-september-2024/) also reported the price as the lowest since September 2024.

Bitcoin peaked at $126,272 on Bitstamp on Oct. 6, 2025. Friday's low sits about 56% below that.

**How borrowed money speeds up a fall**

Traders can bet on bitcoin through futures, putting up a deposit called collateral and borrowing the rest. If the price moves against them far enough, the exchange closes the position and sells automatically. That is a liquidation. Each forced sale can push the price down and set off the next one. About $1.5 billion of crypto futures positions were liquidated in the 24 hours to midday Friday, according to CoinGlass data cited by [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/market-updates/bitcoin-price-crashes-below-59k-crypto-liquidations-top-1-5b/) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/20/bitcoin-plunges-below-usd59-000-as-rush-to-cash-puts-new-bear-market-lows-back-in-play).

**Funds and stocks moved the same way**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had $124.5 million of net outflows on Friday, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/), before BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust posted its figure. On Thursday the funds lost $582.3 million. The Nasdaq composite fell 5.3% on Friday, [AP reported](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-anthropic-ai-chips-boom-c4c3f4878b12989347f8a930ed813dad). Earlier Friday, Fed Governor Lisa Cook said in a [speech](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20261120a.htm) that she doubts September's rate increase will be enough to bring inflation down. The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/), a 0-to-100 gauge of market mood, read 12, or "Extreme Fear."

*In our opinion: the July low was the most visible marker on the chart, and the price is now under it. The traders carrying the most risk are those holding leveraged bets on a rebound, because each new low can force more of them out. Next to watch are Monday's ETF flows and the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, where [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-cook-says-rate-hikes-needed-to-lower-high-inflation-5042321) says markets expect a rate hike.*

articles.title: Fed's Cook Doubts September's Rate Hike Is Enough to Slow Inflation
articles.excerpt: Fed Governor Lisa Cook explained her October dissent in a speech in Chile, saying inflation has topped the 2% target for 67 months and policy is too easy.
articles.body_md:
Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said Friday she is "skeptical that September's single 1/4 point rate increase will be enough to change the path of inflation," in a [speech](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20261120a.htm) in Santiago, Chile.

Cook spoke at the Central Bank of Chile's annual conference. She said inflation has been above the Fed's 2% target for 67 months. She cited estimates that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.8% in the 12 months to October, and 3.2% excluding food and energy.

**Why she voted for a hike in October**

The Fed raised its target range for the federal funds rate to 3.75% to 4% in September, then held it there at its October meeting. Cook was one of two officials who dissented from the hold, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-cook-says-rate-hikes-needed-to-lower-high-inflation-5042321). She said she preferred another quarter-point increase.

She gave two reasons. The first was that financial conditions are "too accommodative." The second was urgency: "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," she said, adding that larger increases might be needed later.

**What "accommodative" means**

The federal funds rate is the rate banks charge each other to lend reserves overnight, [the Fed says](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm). Calling conditions accommodative means borrowing and investing are still easy enough that, in Cook's view, the current rate will add to inflation pressure rather than cool it. Cook said current policy "does not appear to be curtailing the AI buildout," and that rising stock prices keep supporting consumer spending.

She also described the economy as "strong—and accelerating," with third-quarter growth at a 3.4% annual pace and unemployment at 4.1% in October. She said the views were her own and not necessarily those of her colleagues. Financial markets broadly expect a hike at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, Reuters reported.

Bitcoin traded at $56,397 at 11:53 p.m. ET Friday, down 8.2% in 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: Cook is telling markets that one December hike may not be the end of it. That matters for anyone holding assets that pay no interest, bitcoin included, because each hike raises what cash and Treasury bills pay instead. The Dec. 8-9 vote, and how many officials join her case for more, is the next thing to watch.*

articles.title: Wagyu's XMR1 Token Falls 99% After Attacker Sells $13.5 Million
articles.excerpt: An account holding XMR1's deployer key moved 5.2 million tokens and sold part of them on Hyperliquid, Bitquery said. Wagyu's founder blamed a hacked web host and pledged refunds.
articles.body_md:
XMR1, a token that stands in for Monero on the Hyperliquid exchange, fell from about $500 to about $1 on Friday, Nov. 20, after an attacker sold 369,623 tokens to 420 buyers for $13.51 million, according to an [investigation by onchain data firm Bitquery](https://bitquery.io/investigations/xmr1-hyperliquid-hack). [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383732/wrapped-monero-token-collapses-99-after-13-million-hack-blamed-on-web-host) also reported the drop of more than 99%.

**How the token works**

Monero is a privacy coin that runs on its own blockchain, so it can't trade directly on Hyperliquid. Wagyu, a cross-chain swap service, fills that gap: users deposit Monero and receive XMR1, which they can later redeem for real Monero. That makes XMR1 a "wrapped" token, and its value depends on the issuer's reserves and security holding up.

Bitquery said the account that deployed XMR1 sent 5.2 million tokens to an account created that morning, which then sold into the market. The proceeds were moved to Arbitrum, swapped for ether and mostly bridged to Ethereum, and about 7,348 ETH sat in three wallets at Bitquery's last check. Native Monero was not affected, Decrypt reported.

**The web host link**

Wagyu's pseudonymous founder, known as PerpetualCow, said the token's deployer credentials were stolen from 1984.hosting, an Icelandic web host, and that he would personally refund buyers who lost money and relaunch Wagyu, according to Bitquery and Decrypt. He did not give a timeline.

1984 ehf., which runs the host, said in a joint statement with Iceland's national cyber response team, CERT-IS, that it suffered a serious and technically advanced attack and temporarily shut down its services, [DV reported](https://www.dv.is/frettir/2026/11/20/stodva-thjonustu-timabundid-eftir-alvarlega-tolvuaras-a-innvidi-1984-ehf). Its managing director told [RÚV](https://www.ruv.is/english/2026-11-20-serious-cyberattack-thought-backed-by-wealthy-operators-493411) that well-funded attackers were behind it. The statement did not mention Wagyu.

Bitquery said onchain data alone can't show whether the credentials were stolen, and that it can't see how much Monero backs the remaining XMR1.

*In our opinion: the 420 buyers on the other side of those sales carry the loss until a refund actually arrives, so the refund is the number to watch. The deeper lesson is that a wrapped token is only as safe as the credentials that control it, and here those appear to have outlived the server they sat on. Holders of other Wagyu tokens, including ZEC1, which Bitquery says the same deployer account still controls, are the next group with a stake in the post-mortem.*

articles.title: Fairmint Plans Tokenized Stock Venue Under SEC's Innovation Exemption
articles.excerpt: Fairmint said its new subsidiary will trade issuer-sponsored tokenized shares through automated market makers, starting on Canton. Trading hasn't begun, and no launch date is set.
articles.body_md:
Fairmint, a company that records company shares on blockchains, said Friday, Nov. 20, that it plans to run a trading venue for tokenized stocks under the Securities and Exchange Commission's Innovation Exemption, according to its [press release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/20/3407521/0/en/fairmint-announces-plans-for-fairmint-tsv-a-venue-connecting-amms-to-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-shares-with-tradecraft-as-first-amm.html). It would become at least the fifth firm to signal plans under the program.

**What the venue would trade**

The subsidiary, Fairmint TSV LLC, will start on the Canton Network, with Ethereum planned next. It will trade issuer-sponsored shares, meaning the company itself has authorized putting its stock on a blockchain. Fairmint said most tokenized stocks today are tokens that track a share, while its venue trades the share itself.

Trades will run through automated market makers, or AMMs: software that prices and fills orders from pools of assets, with no traditional order book. Tradecraft, a protocol built on Canton, will be the first. Fairmint's SEC-registered transfer agent, Fairmint TA, will verify holders and keep the official ownership record onchain. A transfer agent is the firm that tracks who legally owns a company's shares.

"To trade real shares, they need what every market needs: a clear answer to who owns what, and someone accountable for it," CEO Joris Delanoue said in the release.

**The rules behind it**

The SEC issued the [Innovation Exemption order](https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-trading-markets/innovation-exemption) on Sept. 17, 2026. It gives tokenized securities venues conditional, temporary relief from registering as exchanges. A venue must post a public notice at least 30 calendar days before it operates and then notify the SEC. The agency's list shows four firms that have done so: TSV LLC, OKXICE TSV, Perpetuals.com and Formation Securities. Fairmint is not on it yet.

Fairmint said trading has not begun, and that initial stocks, eligible participants and a launch date will come later, a point [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/20/fairmint-plans-tokenized-stock-venue-on-canton-ethereum-under-sec-experiment) also reported.

*In our opinion: the detail that matters is the transfer agent, because it means buyers would own the share itself, recorded on the company's own register. The 30-day notice rule also sets the clock, since no Fairmint trading can start until a month after its notice goes public. For a market built on instant settlement, the paperwork still moves at the speed of a calendar.*

articles.title: Nasdaq Falls 5.3% and Turns Negative for 2026 as Bitcoin Nears $59,000
articles.excerpt: The Nasdaq composite fell 5.28% Friday and the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% in an AI stock sell-off. Bitcoin traded at $58,970 and ether at $1,617 at 5:54 p.m. ET.
articles.body_md:
The Nasdaq composite fell 5.28% on Friday, Nov. 20, to close at 22,617.73, leaving it down 2.7% for the year, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/stock-market-today-live-updates.html). The S&P 500 dropped 3.7% to 6,910.39, and [Reuters](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-20/nasdaq-plunges-5-a-day-after-anthropic-debut-but-investors-still-believe-in-ai) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-anthropic-ai-chips-boom-c4c3f4878b12989347f8a930ed813dad) reported the same declines.

**Where the selling hit**

Artificial intelligence stocks led the drop. Nvidia fell about 14%, and Anthropic, which listed on Nasdaq a day earlier, closed down about 9%, according to Reuters and CNBC. CNBC said the S&P 500 and the Dow both closed 10% below their records. That is what traders call a correction: a 10% fall from a recent high.

Fund managers quoted by Reuters said they still back the AI trade. "Right now the market is selling first and asking questions later," Michael Monaghan of Founder ETFs told Reuters.

**Crypto in the same session**

Bitcoin traded at $58,970 at 5:54 p.m. ET, down 5.1% in 24 hours, and ether was at $1,617, down 8.1%, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Bitcoin dipped below $58,000 earlier in the day, a high-to-low drop of 31.8% from its Oct. 21 peak, [The Defiant reported](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-falls-below-58-000-but-holds-above-june-low). The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/), which scores market mood from 0 to 100 using price swings, volume and other data, read 12, or "Extreme Fear."

When stocks fall sharply, funds that cut risk can sell crypto along with shares. That is one way crypto and tech stocks can end up moving together, as they did Friday.

*In our opinion: the number to hold onto is 22,617.73, because it puts the Nasdaq's entire 2026 gain back on the table in one session. Crypto didn't decouple; bitcoin and ether both fell with tech, a reminder that in a broad sell-off it trades with the risk crowd. Monday's open, and whether the S&P 500 holds its correction level, is the next test for both markets.*

articles.title: Dollar and Staples Stocks Rise in November as Bitcoin Falls 25%
articles.excerpt: Almost everything fell this month. The dollar, consumer staples and cash funds held up, and Anthropic's IPO took in $119.5 billion while bitcoin ETFs lost $3.47 billion.
articles.body_md:
Almost every major market fell in November. Bitcoin dropped about 25% from its Oct. 31 level to $58,949 at 4:49 p.m. ET Friday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) and [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BTC-USD/history/) data. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 6,910.39, down 3.7% on the day and 10% below its record, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) and the [AP](https://apnews.com/article/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq-c10b797a17c2acf37924d834efebe135) reported.

A short list held up: the U.S. dollar, consumer staples stocks and, this week, Treasury bonds. The money trail is less tidy than "out of crypto, into safety." In the same weeks, investors handed Anthropic $119.5 billion and kept buying stock funds.

**The November scoreboard**

Change from the Oct. 30 close to Friday's close, from Yahoo Finance data, with the Oct. 30 closes checked against [Nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/etf/xlp/historical):

- U.S. dollar index: up 2.0%
- Consumer staples fund (XLP): up 1.2%
- 7-10 year Treasury fund (IEF): down 0.1%
- Dow: down 7.0%
- S&P 500: down 8.8%
- Gold futures: down 9.6%
- Nasdaq Composite: down 11.1%
- Ether: down about 29%, Oct. 31 to Friday afternoon

**How it works: where money goes when prices fall**

A falling price does not send dollars anywhere. Every sale has a buyer, so the cash only changes hands. If bitcoin drops 25%, holders lose value on paper, but no pile of cash leaves the market. Flows are different. They count dollars that actually moved into or out of a fund, a stablecoin or a share sale. That is why this story tracks both.

**The dollar**

The dollar index reached 103.9 on Thursday, its highest since April 2025, and was up 1.7% for the month by Friday midday, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/dollar-price-currency-euro-yen.html) and [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/dollar-near-19month-peak-as-ai-jitters-sap-risk-appetite-5040494) reported. Its rally picked up on Nov. 10 after hot inflation data and Fed Governor Christopher Waller's call to weigh a half-point December hike. Higher expected rates make cash in dollars pay more.

**Treasuries and grocery stocks**

Bond buyers showed up Friday. The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 12 basis points to near 4.93%, its biggest drop in a month, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/treasury-yields-bonds-inflation.html) and [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/5f374b32b07b/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-11-20/) reported. Bond prices rise when yields fall. The long-dated Treasury fund TLT gained 2.6% for the week, though it is still slightly down for November.

Consumer staples led the S&P 500 on Friday, with General Mills, Walmart and Costco higher while chip stocks fell, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/stocks-moving-the-most-today-live-updates.html) and [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/etfs/sector-etfs/26/11/63482468/defensives-lead-sectors-friday-as-growth-trails) reported. People buy cereal and toothpaste in a slump, so these companies' sales often hold steadier.

**Gold did not catch the bid**

Gold fell too. Spot gold was $3,521.38 an ounce at 4 p.m. ET Friday, down 9.3% in a week, [USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/investing/2026/11/20/gold-price-on-november-20-2026/92874871007/) reported. It sits about a third below its Jan. 29 record close of $5,405, [GoldPrice.com](https://goldprice.com/gold-price-today) data show. Gold pays no interest, so rising rate-hike bets and a stronger dollar weigh on it.

**Cash: a record, then a pause**

U.S. money market funds hit a record $8.016 trillion in the week to Nov. 4, the [Investment Company Institute](https://www.ici.org/research/stats/mmf) and [Crane Data](https://k8.cranedata.com/resources/link-of-the-day/) reported. LSEG Lipper counted $117.97 billion of inflows that week, the most since May, citing midterm caution and AI spending worries, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/caution-over-midterms-and-ai-cash-burn-drives-surge-in-us-money-market-fund-inflows-5007303) reported. Crane's daily series shows money funds up $67.7 billion for the month through Nov. 18. The rush has paused: ICI showed a $3.58 billion dip in the week to Nov. 18.

**The biggest buyer: Anthropic's IPO**

Anthropic closed its IPO on Friday. It sold 1.127 billion shares at $83 for $93.5 billion and took in $26 billion more from a private sale to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC, [its release](https://www.anthropic.com/news/ipo-close) and [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/anthropic-ipo-greenshoe.html) said. That is $119.5 billion in all. The stock closed Friday at $88.91, down 8.5% on the day but above its $83 offer price.

**Dip buyers in stock funds**

Investors put a net $59.23 billion into global equity funds in the week to Nov. 18, the most since mid-June, including $12.3 billion into technology funds, LSEG Lipper data show, per [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/global-equity-funds-attract-inflows-for-a-ninth-straight-week-5041603) and [U.S. News](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-20/global-equity-funds-attract-inflows-for-a-ninth-straight-week). That money went in before Thursday's and Friday's selloff.

**What left crypto**

- Spot bitcoin ETFs: $3.47 billion out from Nov. 2 to Nov. 19, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show, matching [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bitcoin-plunges-below-60000-on-pace-for-its-worst-month-since-june-2022-162908483.html)'s count of about $3.5 billion.
- Spot ether ETFs: about $973 million out over the same days, per [Farside](https://farside.co.uk/eth/).
- Stablecoins: supply fell from $296.99 billion on Oct. 31 to $283.56 billion on Friday, down $13.4 billion, [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) data show. [SatoshiMacro](https://satoshimacro.com/tools/crypto/markets/stablecoin-supply/) puts Friday's total at $283.6 billion, below the May 17 peak of $312.9 billion.

When a stablecoin is redeemed, the issuer pays out dollars and sells the matching reserves, mostly short-term Treasury bills. So that $13.4 billion went back into dollars.

**What to watch**

The Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report comes next week, and the Fed meets Dec. 8-9. Traders priced about a 92% chance of a quarter-point hike in December on Friday, per CME FedWatch data cited by CNBC. ICI's next money fund report moves to Wednesday, Nov. 25, for Thanksgiving.

*In our opinion: most of the value lost this month vanished in lower prices rather than moving somewhere else. The clearest measured flows went to cash funds early in the month and to Anthropic's record share sale, which by itself took in about 34 times what left bitcoin ETFs. Crypto's own exits were small next to that, but the $13.4 billion drop in stablecoins shows some money leaving the sector altogether. Next week's PCE report is the next test: a hot reading keeps a December hike in play, and this month that has favored the dollar and cash over bitcoin and gold.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 for the First Time Since July
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin traded near $59,500 at 11:51 a.m. ET Friday, down 5.5% in 24 hours, as AI stocks sold off and a crypto sentiment index sat at 12.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/bitcoin-falls-below-60000-level). It traded near $59,500 at 11:51 a.m. ET, down 5.5% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The drop puts bitcoin about 30% below where it stood 30 days ago, near $84,500 on Oct. 21, per CoinGecko data. Yahoo Finance data show the coin down 23% so far in November, which would be its worst month since June 2022, when it fell 38%, [Yahoo Finance reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bitcoin-plunges-below-60000-on-pace-for-its-worst-month-since-june-2022-162908483.html).

**Tech stocks and fund exits**

Reuters tied the move to concerns about high valuations in the AI trade and other risk assets. Chip stocks fell Friday after Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, with Nvidia down about 3.8% and AMD about 5.1% at the time of [Decrypt's report](https://decrypt.co/383702/bitcoin-breaks-below-60k-crypto-fear-greed-index-lowest).

Ether traded near $1,643 at 11:51 a.m. ET, down 7.4% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds lost $582.3 million on Thursday, taking November withdrawals to about $3.5 billion, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data cited by Yahoo Finance.

**How the fear gauge works**

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index scores market mood from 0, extreme fear, to 100, extreme greed. It blends price swings, trading volume, social media activity and other market data. The [Alternative.me](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) version stood at 12 on Friday, in its "Extreme Fear" band. A low reading describes mood; it does not predict the next move.

**The other view**

Fundstrat strategist Sean Farrell said Thursday that signs of a bottom were starting to emerge, but that selling had not yet reached past levels he would call compelling, Yahoo Finance reported.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is $3.5 billion, the November exit from U.S. bitcoin funds. It comes on top of a 30% price drop in 30 days, and the losses sit with fund holders as well as the miners and treasury companies that keep bitcoin on their books. Friday's flow figures from Farside Investors will show whether the exits slowed or sped up.*

articles.title: Hong Kong Bill Would Require Licenses for Four More Crypto Services
articles.excerpt: The Virtual Asset Services bill, gazetted Friday, would put crypto dealing, advice, management and custody under the SFC. First reading is Dec. 2.
articles.body_md:
Hong Kong published a bill on Friday, Nov. 20, that would require firms offering four more types of crypto services to be licensed by or registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), the [government said](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202611/20/P2026112000582.htm).

The Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 covers dealing, advisory, asset management and custody services. Today, Hong Kong's anti-money-laundering law licenses only one crypto activity, running a trading platform, according to [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/20/hong-kong-moves-to-extend-crypto-licensing-rules-to-brokers-advisers-and-custodians) and [Caixin](https://finance.caixin.com/2026-11-20/102507342.html).

**What changes, and for whom**

The bill would amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. Anyone running one of the four businesses in Hong Kong would need an SFC license or registration and would face a fit-and-proper test, a check of a firm's honesty, finances and competence.

Banks and stored-value facility licensees, such as e-wallet operators supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), would also have to register with the SFC before offering crypto services. The bill gives the SFC and the HKMA powers to run the regime.

In plain terms, a custodian holds client crypto for safekeeping, a dealer buys and sells for clients, and an adviser recommends what to buy. Under the bill, each would need its own permission.

**Officials' case for the bill**

Financial Services Secretary Christopher Hui said the bill follows the principle of "same activity, same risks, same regulation." SFC chief executive Julia Leung said it "marks an important milestone in completing Hong Kong's regulatory framework for virtual assets."

The government's release did not say when the new licensing rules would take effect, and no industry response appeared in the reports Black Mint reviewed. The bill is a proposal and is not law yet.

*In our opinion: the question worth chasing is how long current firms get to comply. Brokers, fund managers and custodians already serving Hong Kong clients would need SFC sign-off, and banks would need a second regulator's registration on top of the HKMA. The Dec. 2 first reading in the Legislative Council is the first date on the calendar; transition terms are the detail to watch.*

articles.title: SEC Says Backward Hat Capital Raised $560 Million in Ponzi Scheme
articles.excerpt: The SEC won an asset freeze against the Indianapolis firm, which it says promised crypto-funded forex trading returning at least 6% a month. The CFTC also sued.
articles.body_md:
The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday, Nov. 20, that it obtained a temporary restraining order and asset freeze against Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital, alleging the firm and its co-founders raised about $560 million from more than 2,000 investors in a Ponzi scheme, according to the [SEC's release](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-116-sec-charges-indianapolis-based-backward-hat-capital-its-co-founders-560-million-dollar-offering).

**What the complaint alleges**

The SEC says co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson told investors their money would be converted to crypto assets and used for foreign exchange (FX) arbitrage, run by an "AI-driven" algorithm they said returned at least 6% a month. Arbitrage means profiting from small price gaps between markets.

Instead, the complaint alleges, the defendants paid more than $250 million to earlier investors with newer investors' money and moved more than $220 million to themselves. That pattern is what makes a Ponzi scheme: returns paid from fresh deposits, not profits.

The SEC also charged Johnson's firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson, who it says produced fake "audit reports" for investors. The case was filed in federal court in the Southern District of Indiana.

**Parallel cases**

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission [filed its own complaint](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9328-26) alleging the scheme took in more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants and did little, if any, forex trading. Federal prosecutors in Manhattan charged Williams and Johnson with securities fraud and conspiracy, and both were arrested on Nov. 18, the [IRS Criminal Investigation unit said](https://www.irs.gov/compliance/criminal-investigation/two-individuals-charged-in-600-million-ponzi-scheme).

The charges are allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Black Mint did not find a public response from the defendants or their lawyers in the filings or reports reviewed.

The SEC urged investors to use resources on [Investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/) to check offers before investing.

*In our opinion: the stake is the money of more than 2,000 investors, and the asset freeze is what stands between them and further losses. Promised returns of 6% a month would more than double money in a year, the kind of figure the SEC's own warning flags. The next thing to watch is whether the Indiana court extends the temporary freeze into a longer-lasting order.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $582.3 Million, Their Worst Day of November
articles.excerpt: BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday's exits, pushing November's net outflows from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs to about $3.47 billion.
articles.body_md:
Investors pulled $582.3 million out of U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Thursday, the biggest one-day outflow of November, [Farside Investors data show](https://farside.co.uk/btc/). The month's net outflows now stand at about $3.47 billion across 14 trading days.

That is the third straight session of net selling, after $239.9 million on Tuesday and $306.5 million on Wednesday. Before Thursday, the worst day of the month was Nov. 5, at $430.2 million.

**IBIT carried most of Thursday's selling**

- BlackRock's IBIT: -$541.1 million
- Fidelity's FBTC: -$45.9 million
- ARK's ARKB: -$31.3 million
- Grayscale's GBTC: -$13.9 million
- MSBT: +$49.6 million

IBIT alone made up about 93% of the day's total. U.S. spot ether ETFs lost another $131.2 million on Thursday, $124.2 million of it from BlackRock's ETHA, according to [Farside's ether table](https://farside.co.uk/eth/).

**How the flow number works**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds real bitcoin for its shareholders. When investors redeem more shares than they buy, large brokers called authorized participants hand shares back, and the fund sells or delivers bitcoin to cover them. So an outflow means the fund's bitcoin pile got smaller. Farside tallies each fund's daily net flow in U.S. dollars.

**Prices on Friday morning**

Bitcoin traded near $62,050 at 5:55 a.m. ET Friday, down about 2.8% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether was near $1,757, down about 2.6%. The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) read 12, in its "Extreme Fear" band.

Since launching in January 2024, the funds still show about $53.6 billion in net inflows by Farside's count.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is $541.1 million, because one fund did nearly all the selling on Thursday. Investors who hold bitcoin through a brokerage account have now taken out about $3.47 billion in November. Friday's flow figure is the next one to watch, with five trading days left in the month after it.*

articles.title: Senate Passes DEATH BETS Act to Ban War and Death Prediction Bets
articles.excerpt: The bill, passed by voice vote Thursday, would bar CFTC-registered exchanges from listing contracts tied to war, terrorism or a death. It now goes to the House.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Senate on Thursday passed S. 4035, the DEATH BETS Act, a bill that would ban CFTC-registered exchanges from listing prediction market contracts tied to war, terrorism, assassination or a person's death. It passed by voice vote at 6:47 p.m. ET, according to the [Senate floor log](https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/thursday-november-19-2026/).

The bill now goes to the House. It is not law until the House passes it and the president signs it.

**What the bill would do**

Under the Senate-passed text, a registered exchange could not list or clear a contract that "expressly references" terrorism, assassination, war or U.S. military operations, [RG reported](https://rg.org/news/prediction-markets/senate-passes-death-bets-act-s-4035-war-death-event-contracts) from the passed version. It also could not list a contract expected to settle mainly on someone's death. The version adds U.S. military operations to the bill Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., introduced in March.

A Schiff-Curtis amendment, named for Schiff and Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, adds a rule of construction. It says the bill does not change existing law for other event contracts, including those tied to gaming, according to [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/news/united-states-senate-passes-amended-death-bets-act/) and RG.

**How these markets work today**

A prediction market lets people trade contracts that pay out if an event happens, such as a rate cut or an election result. In the U.S., the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) oversees such exchanges. Under the Commodity Exchange Act, the CFTC can already block war, terrorism and assassination contracts it finds contrary to the public interest, but that call is at its discretion, [Schiff's office said in March](https://www.schiff.senate.gov/news/press-releases/news-sen-schiff-introduces-legislation-to-explicitly-ban-death-and-war-prediction-contracts/). The bill would write the ban into law.

"There is no justification for gambling on lives," Schiff said in that March statement.

**What comes next**

A House companion bill, H.R. 7942, has sat in a House Agriculture subcommittee since April, DeFi Rate reported. The current Congress ends on Jan. 3, 2027. Black Mint did not find public responses to the vote from prediction market operators by 6 a.m. ET Friday.

*In our opinion: the question worth chasing is whether the House moves before Jan. 3, because a bill that stalls there starts over in the new Congress. For exchanges, the stake is a narrow but hard line in law on which contracts they can list. The CFTC would lose some of the case-by-case discretion it has today.*

articles.title: CFTC Chair Says Hyperliquid and Onchain Venues Get No Special Rules
articles.excerpt: Michael Selig said onchain derivatives venues must register as a U.S. exchange or partner with one, citing Backpack, which won three U.S. licenses this week.
articles.body_md:
CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on Thursday, Nov. 19, that onchain venues such as Hyperliquid have two ways to serve U.S. retail traders: register as an exchange or partner with one that already is. He said they would face the same rules as traditional derivatives exchanges, with no exemption for running on a blockchain.

Selig spoke in an interview at The Hill and The Block's Capitol Crypto Forum in Washington, according to [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-19-cftc-chair-selig-hyperliquid-onchain-venues-the-us-444106) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/20/cftc-tells-hyperliquid-and-crypto-rivals-no-special-rules-for-onchain-trading).

**Two doors into the U.S.**

Selig pointed to Backpack as the model for the first route. The crypto exchange gained three U.S. registrations this week: a designated contract market (an exchange), a derivatives clearing organization (a clearinghouse) and a futures commission merchant (a broker that holds customer funds), The Block reported.

The second route is a partnership with a firm that is already registered, which Selig said other platforms are pursuing, according to The Block and [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/regulation/61595). Hyperliquid itself is not available to U.S. customers and has no U.S. approval, [The Crypto Times](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/19/cftc-chair-outlines-regulatory-path-for-hyperliquids-us-expansion/) noted.

**How a perpetual future works**

A perpetual future is a leveraged bet on an asset's price that never expires. Instead of settling on a set date, traders on one side pay the other a small "funding" fee at regular intervals, which keeps the contract price close to the spot price. Selig said derivatives offered to U.S. retail customers must trade on a registered exchange.

**Other side of the debate**

Selig said some in crypto want lighter oversight, and that equal rules are fair to firms that already comply, according to CoinDesk and The Crypto Times. Hyperliquid did not publicly respond to the remarks in the reports Black Mint reviewed.

*In our opinion: the bigger story is the price of admission. A U.S. exchange, a clearinghouse and a broker license are not a weekend project, and Backpack just showed it can be done. For Hyperliquid, the stake is access to U.S. retail traders it cannot serve today. The first CFTC approval of a partner-based Hyperliquid product is the next filing to track.*

articles.title: VanEck Drops Gemini as Custodian of Its Bitcoin, Ether and SOL ETFs
articles.excerpt: SEC filings show Gemini's custody and clearing deals with three VanEck funds end around Feb. 16, 2027. Coinbase Custody stays on.
articles.body_md:
VanEck is ending its custody and clearing contracts with Gemini for three U.S. crypto ETFs, according to three Form 8-K filings with the SEC signed Thursday. The cutoff is on or about Feb. 16, 2027.

The funds are the VanEck Bitcoin ETF ([HODL](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1838028/000183802826000007/hodl-20261116.htm)), the VanEck Ethereum ETF ([ETHV](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1860788/000186078826000005/ethv-20261116.htm)) and the VanEck Solana ETF ([VSOL](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2028541/000202854126000014/vsol-20261116.htm)). VanEck Digital Assets, the sponsor, sent Gemini Trust Company written notice on Nov. 16, the filings say. Coinbase Custody Trust Company will keep serving as a custodian for all three.

**What a custodian does for an ETF**

A spot crypto ETF owns the actual coins. A custodian keeps those coins in secured accounts on the fund's behalf. Under these contracts, Gemini also held each fund's cash and ran a clearing service, which settles the fund's crypto trades with other Gemini customers.

For VSOL, the change reaches staking, too. Staking means locking up tokens to help run the Solana network in return for rewards. The VSOL filing says Gemini's staking addendum ends when its custody agreement does.

**Contracts that date to 2023**

The HODL agreements are dated Oct. 26, 2023, before the SEC [approved](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/gensler-statement-spot-bitcoin-011023) the first U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Jan. 10, 2024. The ether fund's custody deal is dated May 8, 2024, and the Solana fund's is dated June 13, 2025. Gemini will keep servicing all three funds until the cutoff.

Three months of notice. Then the handover.

The filings don't give a reason for the change. They also don't say how much of each fund's crypto Gemini holds today. [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/20/vaneck-drops-gemini-as-custodian-of-its-bitcoin-ether-and-sol-etfs) that it asked VanEck and Gemini for comment on the reasons.

*In our opinion: this is a breakup served by 8-K, with a three-month notice period. Unless VanEck names a replacement, Coinbase becomes the one custodian named in these filings for all three funds, so more of their coins sit with a single provider. VSOL holders have the most open question: who runs the fund's staking after Feb. 16. Watch for a prospectus update before that date.*

articles.title: MoonPay Seeks OCC Trust Bank Charter to Issue and Hold Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: The proposed MoonPay National Trust Bank, based in Miami Beach, would take no deposits and seek no deposit insurance, its OCC application says.
articles.body_md:
MoonPay has applied to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the federal regulator for national banks, to open MoonPay National Trust Bank. The [application](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/digital-assets-licensing-applications/moonpay-national-trust-bank-combined-cv-pa.pdf) is dated Nov. 17, and the OCC [lists it](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/digital-assets-licensing-applications/index-digital-assets-licensing-applications.html) as received Nov. 18.

The bank would offer "fiduciary custody services," stablecoin issuance, redemption and reserve management, and "conversion services as agent," the filing says. It would be based at 407 Lincoln Road in Miami Beach, Florida. It would take no deposits, and under deposit insurance the form reads "No insurance sought."

**How a trust bank differs from a regular bank**

A national trust bank is a narrow kind of bank. It holds and manages assets for clients, but it doesn't take ordinary deposits or make loans. A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a steady value, such as one U.S. dollar. An issuer creates new tokens when clients send dollars, retires them when clients cash out, and manages the reserves that back them.

The application says the bank would serve clients through digital channels, and the Miami Beach office won't be open to the public. Key details, including the business plan, capital and financial projections, are marked confidential.

**Who would run it**

MoonPay Inc, the New York parent, would own the bank outright. Co-founder Ivan Soto-Wright would chair a five-member board and serve as interim president and CEO, the filing says. In the application, MoonPay says it has more than 30 million customers in 180 countries.

The public can comment for 30 days after a notice runs in the Miami Herald, according to the filing. MoonPay's request sits at the top of 15 pending applications on the OCC's digital-asset licensing list, which also includes Galaxy, Ramp, zerohash and Kraken parent Payward. [PANews](https://www.panews.io/articles/01a1f4af-41b0-77d8-ba24-0f5dd5f35a20) also reported the filing. The OCC has not ruled on it.

*In our opinion: this filing moves MoonPay toward the job of holding stablecoin reserves, the money that has to be there when holders cash out. A federal trust charter would put that work under OCC examiners. The detail that matters most, the bank's capital, sits in the confidential exhibits. The next marker is the close of the 30-day comment window after the Miami Herald notice.*

articles.title: Japan's Core Inflation Rises to 2.2%, Its Highest Reading of 2026
articles.excerpt: Power and gas bills drove the rise, while prices excluding energy cooled to 2.2% from 2.4%. Bitcoin was down 3.4% over 24 hours.
articles.body_md:
Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% in October from a year earlier, up from 2.1% in September, the [Statistics Bureau of Japan](https://www.stat.go.jp/data/cpi/sokuhou/tsuki/index-z.htm) said Friday morning Tokyo time, Thursday evening ET. That's the highest reading of 2026.

Economists polled by Reuters had expected 2.3%, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/japan-inflation-cpi-october.html). Headline inflation rose to 2.3% from 2.1%.

**Energy did the lifting**

Energy prices rose 2.2% from a year earlier after falling 0.6% in September, the [bureau's report](https://www.stat.go.jp/data/cpi/sokuhou/tsuki/pdf/zenkoku.pdf) shows. Electricity went from a 2.4% drop to a 1.6% gain, and city gas rose 5.3% after 0.2%. Household energy subsidies expired in September, CNBC said.

Strip out energy and the picture cooled. Prices excluding fresh food and energy rose 2.2%, down from 2.4%. Rice other than the Koshihikari variety fell 29.8%.

**How Japan measures inflation**

The consumer price index tracks what a set basket of goods and services costs each month. Japan's "core" measure leaves out fresh food, because weather swings those prices around. The Bank of Japan aims for 2% inflation. A year ago, core inflation ran at 3.0%; it fell to 1.4% in April and May before climbing back.

**Market reaction**

The Nikkei 225 fell 2.1% after the data, and the yen traded at 159.59 per dollar, CNBC reported. LSEG data put the odds of a quarter-point BOJ hike in December at 72%, per CNBC. Higher Japanese rates raise the cost of borrowing in yen.

Bitcoin traded at $61,410 at 11:54 p.m. ET Thursday, down 3.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the headline rose, but the measure without energy slowed, so October's increase came mostly from power and gas bills. That hands the BOJ a mixed read heading into December. Households carry the near-term cost; yen borrowers carry the rate risk if the hike comes. Tokyo's November CPI on Nov. 27 is the next data point.*

articles.title: Sky's USDS Supply Falls 38% After Report on Illicit-Linked Swaps
articles.excerpt: About $2 billion of USDS left circulation in a day as the token held near $1. Sky said its peg reserve is working as designed.
articles.body_md:
The supply of Sky's USDS stablecoin fell about 38% in one day, to $3.24 billion at 5:47 p.m. ET Thursday from $5.24 billion a day earlier, [DefiLlama data show](https://defillama.com/stablecoin/sky-dollar). The token held its peg, trading at $1.00 on [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/usds).

The exits followed a [CoinDesk report](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/19/north-korean-hackers-used-sky-s-stablecoin-system-putting-billions-at-freeze-risk) Thursday morning on research by risk firm Inca Digital. Inca traced $518 million in transactions through Sky's Peg Stability Module that involved wallets it linked to hackers, sanctioned entities and other illicit actors. Inca tied about $101.9 million of that to North Korean actors, including wallets funded from the February 2025 Bybit hack, according to the report.

**How the reserve works**

The Peg Stability Module, or PSM, is a pool that lets anyone swap Circle's USDC for Sky's USDS or DAI at about one to one. When USDS slips below $1, traders can turn it in for USDC, which pulls the price back up. Circle can freeze USDC; USDS has no such switch. Inca's concern, as CoinDesk reported it, is that the USDC sits in one shared address. A court-ordered freeze could lock the whole pool along with the flagged money.

**One holder drove most of the exits**

More than $1.5 billion in USDC left the PSM after the report, most of it from one large holder whose address is attributed to the Poloniex exchange, [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/19/sky-s-usds-stablecoin-shrinks-35-as-usd1-5-billion-exits-reserves-after-illicit-finance-report), citing blockchain data. The report noted the label doesn't show who started the trades.

**Sky's response**

Sky [said on X](https://x.com/SkyEcosystem/status/2123466923371282791) that the PSM has processed more than $968 billion since launch, so the alleged figures equal about 0.03% of volume. It said the activity ran mostly through third-party platforms, and its own front ends block flagged wallets.

Rune Christensen, founder of Sky, formerly MakerDAO, [wrote](https://x.com/RuneKek/status/2123500695802253539) that USDS is backed by about $10 billion in collateral and that Sky "handled over $2B in outflows in the past day." He said peg liquidity "never dropped below $2B." He added that Sky's Core Council announced a 5.25 million USDS buyback of SKY tokens over seven days.

*In our opinion: the peg held on Thursday while about $2 billion left. The harder question is legal. If a court or police agency ever asks Circle to freeze the pooled USDC, every holder who relies on that pool would share the hit along with the flagged wallets. The next thing to watch is whether Sky adds wallet screening at the protocol level.*

articles.title: Anthropic Closes Day One at $97.17, 17% Above Its $83 IPO Price
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker opened at $111.50 before giving back part of the gain. Its $81.3 billion offering is the largest IPO on record.
articles.body_md:
Anthropic shares closed at $97.17 in their Nasdaq debut Thursday, 17% above the $83 offer price, after opening at $111.50, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-ant-live-updates.html) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/anthropic-ipo-nasdaq-ai-b6a74b8949021207dc162fcc876c4649) reported.

The AI company, which trades under the ticker ANT, raised $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares. That tops SpaceX's record of about $75 billion from June, [AP said](https://apnews.com/article/anthropic-ipo-by-numbers-fdca56f1cda70c9908899057e7e591e6).

**A $14 Slide From the Open**

At the opening price, the company was valued at about $2.01 trillion, according to AP. By the close, its fully diluted market value was roughly $1.8 trillion, CNBC reported. That ranks it behind only Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and SpaceX among U.S. companies, per CNBC.

More than 846 million shares changed hands, CNBC said, compared with 522 million on SpaceX's first day.

**How an IPO price and an opening price differ**

The $83 price was set Wednesday night by the company and its banks. Only investors who got an allocation, mostly institutions, paid it. The opening price comes later, from an auction on the exchange that matches all the buy and sell orders waiting for the first trade.

So the gap matters. Shares bought at $83 closed up about 17%. Shares bought at the $111.50 open closed down about 13%, by our math.

**Why crypto traders noticed**

Bitcoin was little changed on the day. It traded near $62,196 at 5:47 p.m. ET, down about 0.3% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The deal also reached the Federal Reserve's debate. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on a call with reporters that what early holders do with their new access to cash "is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-goolsbee-says-ai-surge-could-strain-us-capacity-overheat-economy-5039887). More money spent can mean more pressure on prices, and that feeds into rate decisions.

*In our opinion: the first day handed out two very different report cards, depending on what time investors showed up. The bigger number is the paper wealth now sitting with early holders, which the Fed says it is watching. The next dates that matter are the lockup expiries, when insiders can first sell, and the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.*
